chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who performed three circuits or fewer of that, then saw blood. He said, 'She maintains her place; when she is purified, she completes the circuit and counts what has passed.'

This is applicable to the optional circumambulation because we have clarified previously that if the obligatory circumambulation falls short of half, it is incumbent upon its owner to restart it from the beginning, and it is permissible for him to build upon it in the optional circumambulation, and in it is sufficiency, if God wills.
And whenever the woman menstruates after completing the circumambulation, she should make up the two rak'ahs of the circumambulation upon her purification from menstruation.
This is indicated by what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if she gets her period during Hajj circumambulation?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between obligatory (fard) and optional (nafl) Tawaf regarding interruption by menstruation, establishing that partial completion suffices for nafl while fard requires restart if less than half is done. The text further specifies the ruling for making up the two rak'ahs of prayer after purification, highlighting the practical application of ritual purity in Hajj rites. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the flexibility of voluntary acts versus the strictness of obligatory ones during the state of hayd.
